_meta: Values for testing floating-point equality. Most decimal fractions cannot be represented exactly in binary floating point -- 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 are all stored as the nearest available binary value, slightly off -- so arithmetic that should be exact in decimal is off by a tiny amount, and comparing the result with == fails. a + b is meant to equal `expected` (0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3) but does not, under ==. accumulate_value added accumulate_times times is meant to equal accumulate_target (0.1 x 10 = 1.0) but does not, because the tiny per-operation error compounds. dyadic_a + dyadic_b is meant to equal dyadic_expected (0.5 + 0.25 = 0.75) and DOES, because those values are exact in binary (sums of powers of two). The operands are the fixture; every sum, its stored value, and the equality/closeness results are computed.
